meta.dataset_note: No entries with reference === 1116 AND type === 'bechina' exist in torahData.js. The dataset for LM2 currently extends only to reference 1105; Torah 116 (reference 1116) has not yet been entered into the dataset. The source text (torah_116.txt) is a narrative teaching reported by Rebbe Nachman about what prominent settlers in Eretz Yisrael told him: before arriving, they could not conceive that the Land of Israel stood in this physical world, given its described holiness; yet upon arrival they saw it was physically indistinguishable from other lands. The Rebbe then draws a sustained analogy (כְּמוֹ כֵן) to the Tzaddik and the Ish Kasher: they too look physically like all other people, yet are in truth 'an entirely different matter.' The word 'בְּחִינוֹתֶיהָ' appears once (paragraph 5: 'בְּכָל עִנְיָנֶיהָ וּבְחִינוֹתֶיהָ') but used as a plural noun meaning 'its dimensions/aspects,' not as the relational equating formula 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y.' Nowhere in the text does the Rebbe write 'X הוא בְּחִינַת Y,' 'X נִקְרָא Y,' or any equivalent ontological equation between two concepts. The structural device is an analogical comparison (mashal), not a bechina declaration: Eretz Yisrael is likened to the Tzaddik in the same way that the physical conceals the spiritual — but the text never says 'Eretz Yisrael IS a bechina of the Tzaddik' or equates any two nodes as sharing the same essential nature. Packages cannot be built from the bechina subgraph because the subgraph is empty.
